chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

A companion of ours went to ask Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who dies among men, among whom there is no mahram. Should they perform ghusl for her while her clothes are on her? He said: “Then that would be brought upon them, but they should wash her hands.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.ثِيَابُهَا: her clothes, mentioned as a possible covering during washing
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person with whom marriage is permanently forbidden, allowing certain bodily handling restrictions to differ
key_terms.كَفَّيْهَا: her two hands, which are to be washed in this ruling
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُونَهَا: they perform the ritual washing of the deceased upon her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies among men who are not her mahrams?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning the handling of a deceased woman when only unrelated men are present. Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام rejects full washing in such a circumstance and instead instructs that only her hands be washed, indicating a limit set by modesty and mahram restrictions.
